plan: Given my value of $40, I aim to bid slightly above the average expected value to maximize profit. Assuming other bidders value the prize similarly, a bid of $30 should be competitive. This allows potential profit if I win, paying the third-highest bid. The risk of overbidding is minimized, as the bid is below my value, ensuring a net gain if successful.

Given the value of $13, I aim to bid conservatively to avoid potential losses. My bid should be lower than my value to ensure a positive net gain if I win. Since the values are independently drawn and equally likely, I'll bid $10 to balance the chance of winning with minimizing potential loss. This ensures if I win, I pay less than my value, maximizing profit.

Given my private value of $17, I aim to bid below this to ensure profit if I win. I will bid $10. This balances the risk of overpaying and the chance of winning. If I win, I pay the third-highest bid, hopefully much lower than my value. I avoid bidding too high to prevent losses if I win at a bid close to my value.
